sampling_model.design: Observational i.i.d. triangular arrays in the centered linear Watson leaky-instrument SEM.
sampling_model.units: Independent draws \(W_i=(Z_i^{\prime},X_i,Y_i)^{\prime}\) with fixed \(d\) and uniformly bounded eighth moments.
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous treatment \(X_i\) with reduced-form relevance \(\|\beta(P)\|_2\geq c_{\beta}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; weak instruments are excluded by the fixed relevance bound.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The covariance blocks use the measurable ridge inverse \(R_n(S)=(S+n^{-2}I_d)^{-1}\) on every original and bootstrap sample. Reduced-form vectors, the regularized score derivative, and its variance are then sample plug-ins; one Gaussian multiplier process supplies the critical value without conditioning on empirical invertibility. The retained bootstrap uses exactly \(B_n\to\infty\) conditionally independent Efron \(n\)-out-of-\(n\) candidates, strict positive-slack retention, an empirical endpoint-pair law, and a Dirac fallback at the original totalized endpoint pair when no candidate is retained.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The resulting bootstrap distributions are asymptotically valid and practically useful.
There exist no locally asymptotically unbiased estimators and no regular estimators for the stated nondifferentiable functionals.
Random sets can cover the entire identified set uniformly over a class of laws.
Bootstrap approximation of an estimated local parameter space yields uniformly valid tests in constrained moment models.
Gaussian multiplier bootstrap consistently estimates maxima of sums of high-dimensional random vectors under stated conditions.
Full differentiability is necessary and sufficient for standard-bootstrap consistency under a Gaussian first-stage limit.
The nonparametric bootstrap is inconsistent for the boundary-constrained normal-mean estimator.
Test inversion gives uniformly valid inference for root-\(n\) constrained optimization estimators drifting toward a boundary.

body.tldr: Taking Watson et al.'s Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7 quadratic sublevel-set identity as a published input, the project begins at tangent contact: raw population square-root endpoints are used only at nonnegative slack and, on the maintained contact and interior classes, the parameter margin removes the intersection with \(K\). The total positive-part plug-in endpoints have a fourth-root Gaussian law, while a fully specified \(B_n\)-draw Efron feasibility-retained bootstrap converges to a random truncated kernel and is not contact-uniform; its measurable zero-retention fallback is uniformly negligible. Every covariance-based sample object is totalized by one measurable \(n^{-2}\) ridge rule. Conditional on resolving the stated uniform multiplier coupling, inversion before the square-root map gives whole-set coverage, \(n^{-1/4}\) contact loss, and \(n^{-1/2}\) fixed-interior loss under one rule, with both rates matched by explicit contact and interior Gaussian LAN paths.

project_justification.gap: Watson et al.'s Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7 provide the \(p=2\) sharp quadratic sublevel-set identity and its raw endpoint representation at nonnegative slack, and their Theorem 4 supplies a feasibility-retained bootstrap workflow. They do not derive the fourth-root contact law, the random retained-resample kernel for the fully specified finite Monte Carlo algorithm, contact-uniform validity, a whole-identified-set score hull, or a minimax loss frontier. Existing boundary and directional-bootstrap theory does not supply those leaky-IV results.
project_justification.niche: The published scalar quadratic score remains regular at tangent contact even though the endpoint square root is only half-Hölder. Calibrating the score before endpoint transformation creates a route to uniform set inference and makes both contact and interior local minimax geometry explicit.
project_justification.fill: The project keeps the identified set as an always-defined \(K\)-restricted sublevel set, proves when its partial raw endpoints are untruncated, derives the fourth-root contact law and the retained random kernel for an exact Efron algorithm with a negligible measurable fallback, proves nonuniformity for the named workflow, constructs an every-sample multiplier score hull using a common ridge convention, and, conditional on the uniform multiplier coupling, matches its adaptive contact and interior loss rates with certified Gaussian LAN converses.

body.related_work: Watson et al. (2024, Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7) supply the exact \(p=2\) quadratic sharp sublevel set and, at nonnegative slack, its intersection of \(K\) with the raw analytic endpoint interval; these enter solely as published inputs. Their Theorem 4 supplies the feasibility-retained endpoint-bootstrap workflow. The exact finite \(B_n\)-draw Efron algorithm, its zero-retention fallback, the contact endpoint law, retained random kernel, nonuniformity result, score hull, and loss frontiers are not attributed to that paper. Andrews (2000) supplies the local boundary-sequence logic, while Fang and Santos (2019) separate a regular Gaussian primitive from a nonsmooth transform; both inform the nonuniformity proof, but the map here is only half-Hölder and the resampling law is selected. Romano and Shaikh (2010) inform the uniform whole-identified-set coverage criterion. Chernozhukov, Newey, and Santos (2023) inform constrained-score inversion, and Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013) inform multiplier coupling and anti-concentration. Li (2025) obtains boundary-uniform inversion for root-\(n\) constrained point estimators but does not treat partially identified sets. Hirano and Porter (2012) rule out regular estimation of nondifferentiable functionals; the leaky-IV LAN theorem strictly sharpens that diagnosis to matched fourth-root and root-\(n\) directed-Hausdorff frontiers. Hong and Li (2020) inform corrected resampling, but their numerical-bootstrap theorem does not cover a uniformly unknown local index for \(x\mapsto\sqrt{x_+}\).
body.technical_internal_limitation: The early kill test is confined to the Gaussian witness under the stated compatibility regime \(C_{\delta}\geq\bar H\) and the explicit covariance, moment, score-variance, relevance, and \(K\)-interiority bounds. It must verify compact-\(h\) whole-set coverage, the random retained kernel for every deterministic \(B_n\to\infty\), and uniform negligibility of the zero-retention fallback before the general multiplier theorem is pursued. Failure of uniform integrability for the score-band radius would preserve coverage but invalidate the expected-loss claims.
body.honest_scope: Watson et al.'s Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7 quadratic sharp-set reduction is a published input: the identified set is always the \(K\)-restricted score sublevel set, whereas its raw square-root endpoints are partial analytic objects defined only at nonnegative slack. The maintained parameter margin removes \(K\)-truncation on the contact-local and fixed-interior classes where endpoint limits are stated. The contribution begins with the exact contact endpoint law, the random retained kernel for the specified \(B_n\)-candidate Efron algorithm, and named-workflow nonuniformity; the algorithm's zero-retention fallback is measurable and uniformly negligible on the witness. The genuinely open content is one observable multiplier approximation strong enough for uniform whole-set coverage and expected adaptive loss over contact-local and fixed-interior laws. The upper hull and its rates are conditional on an affirmative resolution of that question. All finite-sample covariance operations use the stated ridge convention, the directed loss is defined when a random hull is empty, and both Gaussian lower-bound paths have explicit maintained-class membership regimes. The model keeps \(d\) fixed, assumes a known scalar leakage radius, and excludes weak instruments.
